clauses.reason: The operative sentence exempts William T. Marshall from section 204 and continues him in service until August 1, 1937. TERM:EO:7420:14b12ad4d5728752@772bd1f8338930d0, chars 1325–1386, states that limitation. It covers the whole grant rather than setting a performance deadline. Record August 1 inclusive, through the end of that day; the alternative exclusive reading ends when August 1 begins. The quoted statute and employee recital are not independent commands. EO 7629 separately exercises the exemption power and grants a further period, without changing this order's text or shortening its term. No supplied evidence establishes earlier death, voluntary retirement or other separation. Such an event could end actual service or use of the exemption; the text does not make occurrence of that event a condition terminating the time-limited legal grant itself. No actual continued service through the cap is inferred. This is own-terms cessation, not a finding of formal revocation.

research_rationale:
Read ORIGINAL:EO:7420 in full, chars 0–1492, and ACTOR_TEXT:EO:7629 in full, chars 0–1512. The selected original's heading identifies Marshall and compulsory retirement, its closing number is 7420, and its signing date July 20, 1936 agrees with metadata and EO 7629's recital. Preserve its machine_read_government_printed_copy grade; this confirms the working representation only. The inventory contains the complete operative exemption and continuance; the statute quotation is authority, not a separate presidential command. Both operative elements share the August 1, 1937 temporal limitation. The machine until-event label does not convert this calendar sunset into contingent completion: no performance occurrence is needed for the grant's temporal limit to operate. Inclusive-until treatment follows the supplied ruling; disclose the exclusive alternative. EO 7629, signed June 8, 1937, recites EO 7420 as an earlier one-year exemption and independently grants exemption and continuance until August 1, 1938. Nothing strikes, inserts, revokes or amends EO 7420. Consequently neither the later signing date nor its later cap replaces EO 7420's own ending. Earlier death or retirement is not established; do not confuse actual cessation of service with expiry of this grant, or assume that service ended on signing. Accrued rights, if earned, do not preserve operative authority. The supplied held-text full-name search found one continuation lead, which was read completely; the OFR/corpus citation search likewise found one lead. The USC and eCFR searches found no citations within their stated coverage. Together these are adequate bounded counterevidence searches for this narrow personal grant, with the express limitations that the OFR catalog starts in 1937, 85 census orders lack held text, and the USC edition does not reflect enactments after October 9 through the cutoff. Search silence is not affirmative proof of service, biography, statutory continuity or an ending. The positive ending basis is the original's whole-command fixed limit. The held continuation grant under section 204 corroborates the continuing exemption scheme, without independently establishing every intervening statutory event. No supplied source shows a conflicting amendment, earlier revocation or surviving independent command. Original replacement and quotation recheck remain required; this is same-family AI production, not independent review or human certification.
